question.text: The typical sequence of a SIAB disciplinary proceeding against an empanelled SIA for alleged professional misconduct is:

answer.text: Show-cause -> preliminary enquiry -> complaint -> hearing -> decision.
Preliminary enquiry -> complaint -> decision -> show-cause -> appeal.
Complaint -> immediate suspension -> hearing -> decision (no appeal).
Complaint -> preliminary enquiry -> show-cause notice -> hearing -> decision -> appeal.

explanation.text: The Logic: The conceptual sequence of a fair, natural-justice-compliant professional disciplinary proceeding is: (i) complaint, (ii) preliminary enquiry, (iii) show-cause notice setting out the charges, (iv) hearing with opportunity to lead evidence, (v) reasoned decision/order, and (vi) appeal to an appellate authority. By analogy with established professional-disciplinary schemes (e.g., the ICAI Council scheme), this is the logical order. The Trap: The other sequences are either out of order (show-cause before complaint, or decision before show-cause) or violate natural justice (immediate suspension and no appeal). Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) does not explicitly set out a "complaint -> preliminary enquiry -> show-cause -> hearing -> decision -> appeal" sequence for SIAB on the pages reviewed; searches for disciplinary, SIAB, complaint, show-cause, enquiry, and appeal returned no clear hits. The reasoning above reflects general natural-justice / professional-discipline architecture, not a direct workbook citation.
